newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas soft in prompt, volume better again.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas soft in prompt, volume better again.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures were broadly softer on Friday in a session which saw a relatively hefty 250 lots traded. This compares with a total volume of 70 lots for the whole of last week.

July and August gas both traded at 9.995 pence per therm, 0.005 pence down from Thursday's settlement and under the psychologically important 10 pence mark. April 1998 gained 0.26 pence to trade at 11.40 pence but most of the other months were steady to slightly weaker.
Traders said they were also awaiting a tender from Transco to sell summer gas, which a company spokesman said would be issued this afternoon.
Brokers were optimistic about the increase in volume on the IPE.

"For the last few days we have been noticing that the bid/offer spreads are very narrow - two or three pence per therm, except for one or two exceptions. That is as narrow as you find on the OTC market and that is leading people in to trade."
"This is much, much better," he said but added that the volumes still had to live up to the 500-550 lots traded in a day a couple of months ago.
"There is quite a bit of open interest so I assume that people are covering positions."
